builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
summary: The technique replaces task-specific RL training (trial-and-error interaction plus policy optimization) with direct policy synthesis, where an LLM coding agent reads the environment's source code as a readable world model, writes executable decision rules, and refines them from online feedback or offline data. The cost shifts from GPU training and large interaction budgets to LLM API inference, iterative code-generation overhead, and dependence on access to clean, readable environment source code; no multiplicative performance factor is reported. It can fail when the environment is not available as interpretable source code (compiled, proprietary, or stochastic real-world systems), when the LLM misreads dynamics and synthesizes brittle rules, or when feedback-driven refinement overfits limited offline data, leaving the policy less robust than a trained RL policy under distribution shift.
rationale: The method replaces RL training loops with LLM API calls and is feasible on constrained infrastructure, but its advantage is contingent on having readable environment source code, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: LLM policy synthesis from readable world models
